teachingReview.heading: Name the complete product
teachingReview.before: Conventional capsules, oral solution, and enhanced-absorption products differ in bioavailability and approved use. Milligram-for-milligram substitution without review can destabilize exposure.
teachingReview.after: Conventional capsules, oral solution, and enhanced-absorption products differ in bioavailability and approved use. Milligram-for-milligram substitution without review can destabilize exposure. Conventional SPORANOX capsules contain 100 mg; oral solution contains 10 mg/mL and gives greater exposure than capsules at the same dose. The US SUBA formulation TOLSURA contains 65 mg per capsule in a polymer matrix and is explicitly not interchangeable or substitutable with other itraconazole products. Its adult indications are blastomycosis, histoplasmosis, and aspergillosis when amphotericin B is not tolerated or has failed; it is not indicated for onychomycosis. Conventional SPORANOX capsules also have labeled onychomycosis use in non-immunocompromised patients, while the solution is indicated for oropharyngeal and esophageal candidiasis. Enhanced absorption does not establish better clinical outcomes or a universal dose-conversion ratio.

teachingReview.heading: Teach opposing administration rules
teachingReview.before: Conventional capsules are taken with a full meal and depend on gastric acidity. Oral solution is taken without food when possible. Acid suppression, gastric surgery, nausea, and tube feeding can change the plan.
teachingReview.after: Conventional capsules are taken with a full meal and depend on gastric acidity. Oral solution is taken without food when possible. Swallow conventional capsules whole immediately after a full meal; PPIs, H2 blockers and acid-neutralizing medicines can reduce their absorption. Separate acid-neutralizing medicines by at least two hours before or after the capsule. The capsule label describes increased absorption with non-diet cola in specific fasting, low-acidity studies; this does not establish a universal replacement for the full meal. For oropharyngeal or esophageal candidiasis, vigorously swish the solution in the mouth, 10 mL at a time, for several seconds and swallow. TOLSURA must be swallowed whole with food; do not chew, crush or break it. Its label describes increased exposure with acid-reducing medicines, including omeprazole, requiring adverse-reaction monitoring and possible dose reduction. Acid suppression, gastric surgery, nausea and tube feeding require product-specific intake and delivery assessment. Altered anatomy or a feeding tube does not establish one pharmacokinetic effect, capsule manipulation permission, or a universal feed-hold protocol.

teachingReview.after: Itraconazole has negative inotropic potential and a boxed warning for congestive heart failure and cardiac effects. New edema, dyspnea, rapid weight gain, or exercise intolerance requires prompt evaluation and treatment reassessment. Do not use conventional SPORANOX capsules for onychomycosis in ventricular dysfunction or a history of heart failure. For other conventional-capsule indications, ventricular dysfunction requires a benefit that clearly outweighs the risk; oral solution is restricted in this setting to life-threatening or other serious infections. TOLSURA retains careful benefit-risk review and is not a cardiac-safety workaround. Patient instructions advise stopping itraconazole and contacting the healthcare provider immediately for heart-failure symptoms. Conventional capsule clinical labeling calls for discontinuation; solution and TOLSURA clinical warnings require reassessment of continued therapy and alternatives. Review interacting negative inotropes, including calcium channel blockers; felodipine and nisoldipine are contraindicated combinations.

after.question: A patient takes conventional itraconazole capsules fasting with a proton pump inhibitor. What is the main concern?
choices: Reduced and variable absorption with treatment failure risk
Food omission and acid suppression reliably increase conventional capsule exposure
Identical exposure because conventional capsules and oral solution contain the same ingredient
No concern because every itraconazole product is independent of gastric pH
after.rationale: Fasting and proton pump inhibition can reduce conventional capsule absorption and threaten efficacy; they do not guarantee either failure or toxic exposure in an individual patient. Verify the full-meal, whole-capsule instructions and review the acid-suppressing medicine. Oral solution is not dose-for-dose interchangeable, and TOLSURA has different food and pH instructions. Shared ingredients do not establish equal exposure or one pH rule.
